articles.title: Stop trusting your Amazon payout number: check the settlement report line by line in Google Sheets
articles.excerpt: Amazon pays you one number per settlement period. Getting from the lines in the report to that number takes a few checks, and you can do them in a spreadsheet without logging in anywhere else. In Sell…
articles.body: Amazon pays you one number per settlement period. Getting from the lines in the report to that number takes a few checks, and you can do them in a spreadsheet without logging in anywhere else. 1. Download one settlement report In Seller Central go to Finance > Finance reports > Settlement statement reports and download one settlement as a .txt file. It is tab-separated, one row per transaction. 2. Check that the payout adds up Import the file into a blank sheet (File > Import, "Replace data at selected cell"). Sum the amount column over every row and compare it with the total payout the report states. If they differ, you have a line the summary does not show. 3.

articles.title: Fluid sizes with CSS clamp(): practical examples you can copy
articles.excerpt: Media queries make values jump: 16px, then suddenly 20px, then 24px. Fluid values grow smoothly with the screen instead. In modern CSS, one line does it: font-size: clamp(16px, calc(10.66667px + 1.481…
articles.body: Media queries make values jump: 16px, then suddenly 20px, then 24px. Fluid values grow smoothly with the screen instead. In modern CSS, one line does it: font-size : clamp ( 16 px , calc ( 10 . 66667 px + 1 . 48148 vw ), 32 px ); This post shows how to read declarations like this, gives you ready-made examples, and covers the mistakes that quietly break them. How to read a clamp() declaration clamp() takes three arguments: clamp ( minimum , preferred , maximum ) minimum : the value never goes below this (16px above) preferred : the part that changes with the viewport ( calc(… + …vw) ) maximum : the value never goes above this (32px above) The example above means: 16px on a 360px screen, 32px on a 1440px screen, smooth growth in between , and it stays at 16px or 32px outside that range.

articles.title: Treat Your Payment Details Like a Public API: An IBAN in Your Own Name for Developers Paid From Abroad
articles.excerpt: I'm Marco Lopez, CMO at NovoEX. I spend a lot of my week talking with developers who contract for teams in other countries, and one point of friction comes up again and again. It isn't the code, the s…
articles.body: I'm Marco Lopez, CMO at NovoEX. I spend a lot of my week talking with developers who contract for teams in other countries, and one point of friction comes up again and again. It isn't the code, the scope or the deadline. It's the moment after the invoice, when the money has to find its way home. So this post is a practical one. I'll mention what we built at NovoEX in a short section at the end, but everything before that applies no matter where you bank. Your payment details are an interface Here's the mental model I keep coming back to. The bank details you paste into an invoice are a public interface. Your client's finance team is the consumer of that interface, and they integrate with it once, store it in their vendor system, and then call it every month.

articles.body: Your search box works fine in dev. In production, users type fast, the network is uneven, and suddenly the results on screen don't match what they typed. articles.title: I built a hand-drawn React UI kit that's crooked on purpose and accessible anyway
articles.excerpt: Most UI kits try hard to look neutral. PlopUI goes the other way: wobbly sticker buttons, washi-tape tags, a hand-lettered marker font, colors picked by instinct. The whole thing looks like it was dra…
articles.body: Most UI kits try hard to look neutral. PlopUI goes the other way: wobbly sticker buttons, washi-tape tags, a hand-lettered marker font, colors picked by instinct. The whole thing looks like it was drawn on the back of a receipt. It has one rule: break the visual rulebook, never the accessibility one. The drawing sits on top, never instead A PlopUI button is a real <button> . A checkbox is a real checkbox. The hand-drawn outlines, shadows and doodles are decoration layered over native elements, so the browser and screen readers still know exactly what everything is. That means the boring stuff just works: Tab, Enter and Space do what you expect. Select and Menu also handle arrow keys, Home, End, type-to-jump and Escape.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 2, 2000: Expedition 1 Arrives at the International Space Station
articles.excerpt: Expedition 1 crewmates Bill Shepherd, Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev pose with a model of the space station as it appeared in 2000.
articles.body: On Nov. 2, 2000, the International Space Station welcomed its first long-term residents: NASA astronaut Bill Shepherd and two Russian cosmonauts, Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev. The mission was called Expedition 1. Before this expedition, NASA had launched five, one-week-long Space Shuttle missions to help build the space station and bring up supplies. But this time, the crew would be staying for four and a half months, and they weren't taking the shuttle. Instead, they took a Russian Soyuz spacecraft , and this was the first Soyuz to ever dock at the space station. During their stay at the space station, they unpacked supplies and installed new equipment, including the first solar arrays.

articles.excerpt: In this image, we can see a colorful view of an ancient, rocky Martian hill.
articles.body: In this image, we can see a colorful view of an ancient, rocky Martian hill. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UArizona) This rainbow-hued rocky plain looks like the landscape of an alien world. And, it turns out, it is. What is it? In this image, we can see an ancient, rocky hill on Mars . In the Red Planet's Southern Highlands, this alien terrain is chock-full of minerals, which we can see clearly defined in this color-enhanced view of the region. This image was snapped by the HiRISE camera aboard NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter ( MRO ), which has been studying the planet's surface, atmosphere and climate since arriving in Martian orbit in March 2006. But this isn't exactly what the surface of the planet would look like through our eyes; the image is color-enhanced.

articles.title: What is Starshield? A look at SpaceX's military satellite network
articles.excerpt: SpaceX is building and operating two satellite networks at the moment, Starlink and Starshield. What’s the difference between the two, and who uses them?
articles.body: SpaceX is building and operating two satellite networks at the moment, Starlink and Starshield. What’s the difference between the two, and who uses them? For more than a week in October 2026, Ukrainian drone operators found their high-speed satellite links shut off. Officials in Kyiv said that terminals for SpaceX ’s Starshield network stopped working at speeds of above 160 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour) from Oct. 14, hampering efforts to conduct defensive operations and intercept Russian drones. Full connectivity was restored on Oct. 24, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The arguments over who did what continue, but the affair highlighted how little is publicly understood about Starshield — what it is, how it relates to Starlink , and how it is operated.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
